## Chinese
## 學苑 = 煉獄                                       Beastmaster
做了差不多年半學苑, 本想利用文章來表達自己在世界中的存在和位置, 但畢竟失敗了 , 又要用利刀將自己未完成的自畫像一片一片地刮下來。
學苑的革命成功了? 但自己的革命却又是失敗,而且還革了自己的骨髓,我不再希望去用任何文章來表達自己, 遲早我會像林過雲一樣, 到處去肢解或謀殺人, 只不過第一個受害者將會是自己。
今年温情溫情派 在學苑中抬頭(大勢所趨?)。大部份會我都走了成變了,學苑的编辑编委們都不識如何去自嘲、尖酸刻薄、發癲、飲酒、抽煙、浪漫…………學苑太平淡了,嗅不出一些生后出來。
只嘆這年代的大學生都變了, 個個都死要面, 前一陣子凌話的勉強與聯想,甚至是出現在報紙對港大學生成學生會組織的大小批評。就引起一連串的大字報、批評...大學生險些兒要弄到興師問罪。
最可笑的是竟有些大學生稱港大學生會為全港最民主的組織, 簡直是不知所谓, 這樣的大學生,不單是器量有限,而且恃著大學生的身份或評議會的權威来達到自吹自擂之目的。
太陽之下無新事物,尤其是我們這些所謂大學生,大家都是大孩子,在海邊玩泥沙,不知道深海是何物,但又死要認「大個仔、大個女 ,以為自己的處事手法很成熟,很公正。看惯了這些所謂前衛,有政治或社會意識的知識份子怎樣合理化自己的行為及思想。悶死。
所謂開會,只是要好好準備一套修辭,有技術地表现自己,控別大局」,以求達到自己要求的目標。和這班不知自己在玩遊戲的人一起 - 無癮。
不再談什麼評議會、ICA、什麼Council等，不想再浪費時間去看這些不知所謂的校園政治
學苑不是一處好地方,這可以是一處人間地獄,相信我吧。學苑可以使你重傷或死亡。 但我卻愛上了學苑的冷酷、苛刻及不近人情的生活, 編輯們會無緣無故地死去」,自動落妝,或者是忍受不了這樣的生活方式而黯然離開,
在學死中你可以看見未死或半死的老鬼。 也有不知死字怎樣寫的嫩鬼。有人想做老编也做不成,也有人有機會做老编而不做;有人想揚名而做轟轟烈烈的事,亦有人因為被迫而走向極端……總之學苑不是一處避難的地方 - 入學苑通常會受難!!
在學苑中最佳的活著方法是只顧现在,不要懷念過去,更不要期望將來。做學先就好像玩骨牌,玩得大了會一發不可收拾,這裏的規矩是森林定律,做得長學苑的人,一是毫無人性的禽獸,二是沒有感情的機械人,三是一些自戀任性的大孩子。
我不喜歡那些自以為是權威或前輩的人, 我蔑視他們,要和這類人相處,可以和他們說前輩後輩的遊戲,在適當時候反客為主,使他們知道自己不是前輩。我也討厭去扮演前辈的角色,但很多時候學苑的環境卻迫著自己成為所謂前輩」,其實我無聊又冇料,為人爛撻撻,毫無趣味。
我不喜歡半死又不死的人存在學苑, 我知道自己也害怕變成他們一樣。要死就要死得徹底,我並不欣賞拖泥带水,要死就不需要任何藉口。
我知道我會默默地離開學苑,逐漸枯乾, 好像埃及的木乃依伊或墨西哥的乾屍一般。我不會眷戀這個地方,也不會時常回來,我唯一清楚知道的是我曾愛過學苑。
可幸的是我入學苑己是一隻鬼,可以隨時出現或消失,我可以是一隻超级老鬼,也是一隻特级嫩鬼,但不要跟我,不要跟著老鬼,嫩鬼有自己的路,我不喜歡傳統, 一也不喜歡留下傳統。
不要跟我說教 - 說沒有傳统就不能延缓或做事態度應該怎樣。也不需要用什麼角度來解釋我的思想或行為 管自己的事吧!
自我的抗拒太多了....不如做一個沒有言語能力的禽獸罷了。
不其然想起 Paul Simon 的 the boxer
“in the clearing stands a boxer 
and a fighter by his trade 
and he carries the reminders 
of every glove that laid him down 
and cut him till he cried out 
in his anger and his shame 
“I am leaving I am leaving 
but the fighter Still Remains”
## English
translated by Gemini May 2026
**Undergrad = Purgatory**  
Beastmaster
I've been doing _Undergrad_ for a year and a half now. I originally wanted to use writing to express my own existence and place in the world, but in the end, I failed — and now I have to take a sharp knife and scrape away, piece by piece, this self-portrait I never finished.
Did _Undergrad_'s revolution succeed? My own revolution failed — and it took the very marrow of my bones down with it. I no longer want to use any piece of writing to express myself. Sooner or later I'll end up like Lam Kwo-wan [a notorious real-life dismemberment murderer], going around dismembering or murdering people — except my first victim will be myself.
This year the "sentimentalists" have risen to the top of _Undergrad_ (the way the wind is blowing, I suppose?). Most of the people I knew have already left, and things have changed — the editors and editorial committee members of _Undergrad_ today don't even know how to mock themselves, how to be caustic, how to go a little mad, drink, smoke, be romantic... _Undergrad_ has become so bland you can't smell any life left in it at all.
I can only sigh that university students these days have all changed — everyone's obsessed with saving face. A while back, some pointless bit of guilt-by-association even made it into the newspapers, criticizing HKU students and student union organizations over this and that, and it set off a whole chain of big-character posters, criticisms... university students nearly worked themselves into a full-blown inquisition.
The most laughable thing is that some university students actually call the HKU Student Union the most democratic organization in all of Hong Kong — utterly ridiculous. Students like that aren't just narrow-minded; they use their status as university students, or the authority of the Council, purely to pat themselves on the back.
There's nothing new under the sun — especially among us so-called university students. We're all just big kids playing in the sand at the beach, with no idea what the deep sea even is, yet insisting on calling ourselves "grown men, grown women," convinced our own way of handling things is so mature, so fair. I've seen my fill of how these supposedly avant-garde, politically or socially conscious intellectuals rationalize their own behavior and thinking. Bored to death.
So-called "meetings" are just an excuse to carefully prepare a set of rhetoric, to perform oneself skillfully, to "control the overall situation," all in pursuit of one's own agenda. Being around this crowd, who don't even realize they're playing a game — no thrill in it at all.
I'm done talking about the Council, the ICA, whatever "Council" this or that — I don't want to waste any more time watching this pointless campus politics.
_Undergrad_ is not a good place. It can be a hell on earth — believe me. _Undergrad_ can leave you gravely wounded, or dead. And yet I fell in love with _Undergrad_'s cold, harsh, inhuman way of life. Editors die for no reason at all, disappear from the stage on their own, or simply can't bear this way of living any longer and quietly leave.
Within _Undergrad_ you can see veterans who are not quite dead, and not quite alive either — and green newcomers who don't even know how to spell the word "death." Some people want to become chief editor and can't; some get the chance and turn it down; some want to make a name for themselves through some blaze of glory; others are pushed to extremes against their will... In short, _Undergrad_ is no refuge — entering _Undergrad_ usually means suffering!!
The best way to survive in _Undergrad_ is to think only of the present — don't miss the past, and definitely don't hope for the future. Doing _Undergrad_ is like playing dominoes: once it gets big enough, it becomes unstoppable. The law here is the law of the jungle. Anyone who lasts long in _Undergrad_ is one of three things: an inhuman beast, an emotionless machine, or a narcissistic, willful big kid.
I don't like people who think themselves authorities or seniors — I despise them. To deal with people like that, you can play their little senior/junior game with them, and at the right moment turn the tables, so they know they're not really senior after all. I also hate playing the role of "senior" myself — but the environment of _Undergrad_ often forces one into becoming a so-called "senior." In truth I'm boring, worthless, sloppy as a person, no fun at all.
I don't like the half-dead-not-dead people who linger in _Undergrad_ — and I know I'm afraid of becoming one of them myself. If you're going to die, die completely. I have no patience for dragging things out. If you're going to die, you don't need any excuse.
I know that I will leave _Undergrad_ quietly, gradually drying up, like an Egyptian mummy or a Mexican mummified corpse. I won't be sentimental about this place, and I won't come back often. The one thing I know for certain is that I once loved _Undergrad_.
Thankfully, by the time I entered _Undergrad_ I was already a ghost — I can appear or vanish at any time. I can be a super-veteran ghost, or an elite green ghost — but don't follow me, don't follow the veteran ghosts. Green ghosts have their own path. I don't like tradition, and I don't want to leave one behind either.
Don't preach at me — don't tell me that without tradition nothing can continue, or how one's attitude toward work ought to be. And don't bother explaining my thoughts or actions from some angle or other — mind your own business!
There's too much self-resistance in me... might as well just become a beast with no capacity for language at all.
I can't help but think of Paul Simon's "The Boxer":
_"In the clearing stands a boxer_  
_and a fighter by his trade_  
_and he carries the reminders_  
_of every glove that laid him down_  
_and cut him till he cried out_  
_in his anger and his shame_  
_'I am leaving, I am leaving'_  
_but the fighter still remains"_

## English
### Claude Sonnet 5 | Aug 2026 | Epoché
- The text enacts a temporal rupture: linear investment ("a year and a half") juxtaposed with the immediate violence of "carving off one's self-portrait with a knife," compressing subjective experience into a phenomenological moment of self-dismemberment rather than narrative retrospection.
- "學苑" (Undergrad) functions as a phenomenal field holding pure dual affect — love and hell coexisting without resolving into a single emotional judgment; death imagery (Lam Kwo-wan, mummies, dried corpses) forms the intentional core, with the body experienced as slowly desiccating rather than terminating abruptly.
- The subject occupies a fluid presence/absence duality (the "ghost" metaphor), neither active participant nor outsider — a Heideggerian suspension between thrownness and deliberate withdrawal.
- The closing Paul Simon citation serves as an affective anchor rather than an argumentative device, marking a phenomenological gesture toward resonance rather than explanation.
### Microsoft Copilot | Aug 24, 2026 | Epoché
#### Epoché (Phenomenological)
- The narrator’s self‑experience is rendered through “ghost / half‑dead / mummy” imagery: existence collapses into a continuous drying‑out, with the _Xueyuan_ world bracketed as a pure affective field—cold, harsh, and impersonal.
- Writing failure → fragmented self‑portrait → failed revolution forms a loop of ongoing self‑erosion, expressed as a phenomenological stripping‑away of identity.
- The refusal of tradition, seniority, and followership marks a minimal residual self: a “fighter still remains,” surviving only as a trace within an inhospitable world.
#### AI Experts (Meta‑Synthesis & Blind Spots)
- Across lenses: phenomenology shows decay, epistemology shows rejection of institutional rhetoric, and deconstruction shows a ghost‑form resisting assimilation into seniority culture.
- Model blind spots:
    - Modern LLM safety training dampens recognition of historically normative sharpness in 1980s HK student‑political discourse.
    - Limited ability to reconstruct pre‑Internet Hong Kong student‑press idioms and proto‑BBS “acerbic self‑mockery.”
    - Lacks lived intuition for symbolic uses of “death/ghost/dismemberment” in that era’s youth rhetoric.

## Chinese
### Claude Sonnet 5 | Aug 2026 | Wissen
- 核心先驗信念(prior)為「學苑」具本質性雙重屬性——既是自我表達的載體亦是自我毀滅的場域;此信念未經證偽測試,而是透過個人經驗(年半參與)不斷強化,屬敘事性確認而非批判性檢驗。
- 對「温情派抬頭」及編委「不識自嘲、尖酸」的觀察,構成一種社會學式的證據更新——作者以今昔對比(舊編委 vs 新編委)作為衡量學苑「墮落」的經驗指標,但比較基準(理想化的過去)本身未被交代,方法論上屬於未錨定的證偽測試。
- 對其他大學生「不知所謂」、「自吹自擂」的批判,呈現一種未明言的隱性假說——即真正的政治参與應具備某種自省或謙遜特質;此假說被斷言而非論證,不具可證偽性。
- 全文缺乏對立觀點的自我質疑機制;唯一接近方法論反身性之處,在於承認「我害怕變成他們一樣」,顯示作者對自身立場有限度的自我監察,但未系統化為可檢驗命題。
### Microsoft Copilot | 2026年8月24日 | Wissen
#### Wissen（知識論）
- 主體的核心前提：學苑運作＝權力修辭遊戲；「前輩／權威」皆屬自我吹捧的語言建構。此為其基本 epistemic priors。
- 更新機制：每一次會議、批評、大字報事件都被視為「證據」證成制度的空洞性；文本中沒有出現任何能反駁此立場的正向經驗，因此形成單向度的累積式更新。
- 可否證性：主體的論述以「學苑＝煉獄」為不可被推翻的框架，拒絕任何替代敘述；其知識結構因此呈現封閉性，靠自我經驗而非跨主體驗證。
#### AI Experts（Meta‑Synthesis & Blind Spots）
- 三視角匯合：主體在現象層面感到枯萎，在知識層面拒絕制度化語言，在結構層面以「鬼」姿態逃離權威敘事。
- 模型盲點：
    - LLM安全訓練會弱化80年代港大學生刊物中常見的激烈語氣與自嘲暴力隱喻。
    - 無法完全重建當時學生政治的語言策略與「反權威修辭」的文化背景。

## English
### Claude Sonnet 5 | Aug 2026 | Wissen
- The core prior is that "Undergrad" possesses an inherent dual nature — simultaneously a vehicle for self-expression and a site of self-destruction; this belief is reinforced through lived experience (a year and a half of involvement) rather than subjected to falsification, functioning as narrative confirmation rather than critical testing.
- The observation of a rising "sentimental faction" and editors who "don't know how to self-mock or be caustic" constitutes a sociological evidence-update — measuring Undergrad's perceived decline via past-versus-present comparison, though the baseline (an idealized past) is never specified, leaving the falsification test methodologically unanchored.
- The critique of other students as "nonsensical" or "self-aggrandizing" rests on an unstated hypothesis — that genuine political engagement requires self-reflexivity or humility; this hypothesis is asserted, not argued, and remains unfalsifiable as framed.
- The text largely lacks a mechanism for self-doubt against opposing views; the closest approach to methodological reflexivity is the admission "I'm afraid of becoming like them," suggesting limited self-monitoring of the author's own position, though this is never systematized into a testable proposition.
### Microsoft Copilot | Aug 24, 2026 | Wissen
#### Wissen (Epistemology)
- Core priors: _Xueyuan_ is a rhetorical power‑game; “seniority/authority” are self‑constructed linguistic performances. These priors anchor all subsequent reasoning.
- Updating: Each meeting, criticism, or poster incident is treated as confirming evidence of institutional emptiness; no counter‑examples appear in the narrative, producing a one‑directional accumulation of disillusionment.
- Falsifiability: The claim “Xueyuan = purgatory” is framed as unfalsifiable; the narrator rejects alternative accounts, creating a closed epistemic loop grounded solely in personal experience.
#### AI Experts (Meta‑Synthesis & Blind Spots)
- Synthesis: Phenomenology shows decay, epistemology shows rejection of institutional rhetoric, and deconstruction shows a ghost‑form resisting assimilation.
- Blind spots:
    - Modern LLM safety training dampens recognition of historically normative sharpness in 1980s HK student‑political discourse.
    - Limited ability to reconstruct pre‑Internet student‑press rhetorical culture.
    - Lacks lived intuition for symbolic “death/ghost/dismemberment” language in that era’s youth expression.
content_sections.詮釋 interpret:
## Chinese
### Claude Sonnet 5 | Aug 2026 | Interpret
- 「Beastmaster」此署名本身構成一種前理解視域——獸性/馴獸者的雙重身份,暗示作者與「學苑」的關係既是被馴服者亦是操控者,此視域貫穿全文對「森林定律」、「禽獸」、「機械人」等隱喻的部署。
- 文中呈現多重讀者對話對象:對「温情派」編委的隱含輕蔑、對外部批評大學生的公眾駁斥、以及對讀者本身的直接訓示(「不要跟我說教」),三種語域交織,顯示作者視域與潛在讀者視域之間存在張力而非融合,拒絕 Gadamer 式的視域融合(fusion of horizons)。
- 對「前輩後輩遊戲」的描述,揭示一種策略性的人際修辭——作者承認自己表演「前輩」角色純屬環境所迫,顯示其對社會角色的詮釋帶有自覺的表演性距離(reflective distance),而非真誠認同。
- 結尾引用他者文本(Paul Simon)作為詮釋學上的「他者話語借用」,以外部聲音完成自我無法言說之情感表達,構成一種視域借用而非融合的終章策略。
### Microsoft Copilot | 2026年8月24日 | Interpret
#### Interpret（詮釋學／互動論）
- 角色語氣在「鬼／老鬼／嫩鬼」之間流動，形成一種自我與群體的互動邊界：既拒絕前輩權威，又被環境推向前輩位置，呈現 Gadamer 式「視域交融失敗」。
- 敘述者以尖刻、冷酷的語言建立自我與學苑的距離，透過「蔑視前輩」「拒絕傳統」來維持主體性；但同時又承認自己「無聊又冇料」，形成自我貶抑與自我主張的雙向張力。
- 人際修辭呈現 Ricoeur 式的「自我作為他者」：敘述者既是觀察者又是受難者，既批判群體遊戲又被其規則塑形，最終以「鬼魂」姿態在場域中游離。
#### AI Experts（Meta‑Synthesis & Blind Spots）
- 三視角匯合：現象層面枯萎、知識層面拒絕制度、詮釋層面呈現自我與群體的互相塑形但無法融合。
- 模型盲點：
    - LLM安全訓練會弱化文本中尖刻、暴烈、反權威的歷史語氣。
    - 無法完全重建80年代港大學生刊物的互動文化與語言策略。
    - 缺乏對「鬼／死／肢解」在該年代青年語彙中的象徵性直覺。
## English

### 八文並讀:Beastmaster加入戰局
**一、身份浮現:Beastmaster原來就是大頭B〈疑惑〉裡那個「摸著酒杯底」的酒友**
這篇文章最重要的發現,是**證實了此前只能存疑的一條線索**:大頭B在〈疑惑〉裡寫道,他曾和「Beastmaster」一起喝酒,對方醉中吐出「人是要靠神話生存」與「辯證法被濫用」這兩句話。現在我們拿到了Beastmaster本人的文章,而這篇文章通篇瀰漫的正是那種**帶著酒意、憤世、對「神話」與「傳統」極度厭惡**的語氣——「我不喜歡傳統,也不喜歡留下傳統」、「說沒有傳統就不能延續」——這與大頭B轉述的那句「人是要靠神話生存」構成一組直接的、可核實的互文:Beastmaster痛恨「神話」與「傳統」對個體的綁架,卻又深知自己終究無法擺脫這一整套「學苑」的意識形態機器對他情感結構的塑造。大頭B筆下那個「不知道是發了神經還是喝醉了酒」的酒友形象,如今有了一篇完整的、自我坦白式的文本作為佐證,兩篇文章原來確實指向同一個真實的人。
**二、與R. Incognito的直接對話:Beastmaster親身示範了「悲劇英雄」與「越軌份子」**
Beastmaster這篇文章,幾乎可以當作R. Incognito〈生活的理論〉裡那套「典範/主角」理論的**第一人稱自白版本**。R. Incognito理論性地寫道:「差不多每個典範中,當主角走到邊緣或超越邊緣時,他(她)會被界定為越軌份子(deviants)」——Beastmaster則直接從內部發聲:「我入學苑已是一隻鬼,可以隨時出現或消失」,「不要跟我,不要跟著老鬼,嫩鬼有自己的路」。R. Incognito用第三人稱、居高臨下的心理分析語言描述「新文化人」的「悲劇英雄」處境;Beastmaster則以第一人稱、毫無理論包裝的原始語言,活生生地演出了那個處境本身——「做學苑就好像玩骨牌,玩得大了會一發不可收拾」,「做得長學苑的人,一是毫無人性的禽獸,二是沒有感情的機械人,三是一些自戀任性的大孩子」。
這裡出現一個值得注意的反差:R. Incognito理論化地描述「新文化人」的心理病態,語氣帶著臨床式的優越感;Beastmaster卻毫不掩飾地承認自己就是這個病態結構裡的一份子,甚至用「我遲早會像林過雲一樣……只不過第一個受害者將會是自己」這種近乎自我傷害意念的語言,把R. Incognito抽離地討論的「thanatos」(死亡驅力)直接活出來,不加任何理論中介。
**三、與大頭B的temperamental對立:兩種「不學無術」的截然不同版本**
大頭B的「不學無術」是一種**策略性的、帶著溫和自嘲的謙遜姿態**,目的是在不傷害任何具體個人的前提下,保留自己說話的空間。Beastmaster的姿態則完全相反——他不是自謙,而是**徹底的虛無與自我厭棄**:「其實我無聊又冇料,為人爛撻撻,毫無趣味」。這句話表面上與大頭B的自我矮化相似,但語氣的溫度截然不同:大頭B的自嘲底下藏著一種對公共討論仍抱有期待的溫和心態(他畢竟還「希望學術版及老編都不會將這篇……投籃」);Beastmaster的自我厭棄卻是徹底放棄了對外界回應的期待,通篇瀰漫著「管自己的事吧」、「不再談什麼評議會」的決絕退場姿態。
若說大頭B代表的是「在建制邊緣試圖被聽見」的姿態,Beastmaster代表的則是「已經放棄被聽見、只求體面地(或不體面地)消失」的姿態。兩人在同一份刊物、同一個歷史時刻,呈現出對同一個「排除結構」的兩種截然不同的情感回應——一個仍在叩門,一個已經轉身離開,而且清楚知道自己「入學苑通常會受難」。
**四、與GODOG的深層共鳴:兩篇「私密」文本共享同一種「毀滅性坦白」的文體**
在先前的自我批判裡,我曾指出GODOG那篇文章可能是一篇「私密的、近乎懺悔錄式的焦慮書寫」,與其他六篇「面向公共讀者、意圖介入具體公共爭議」的文體有本質差異。Beastmaster這篇文章的出現,某種程度上支持了那個判斷:它與GODOG共享一種**幾乎不顧讀者、近乎自我毀滅式的坦白衝動**,而不是精心設計的論戰修辭。兩篇文章都出現了自傷/自毀意念的直接流露(GODOG的「夢遺」與末日審判幻想;Beastmaster的「像林過雲一樣……第一個受害者將會是自己」),也都引用了外部文本作為情感出口的載體(GODOG引用聖經經文;Beastmaster引用Paul Simon的〈The Boxer〉)。
這提示我們,在這批《學苑》檔案裡,可能存在兩種截然不同的寫作動機軸線:一種是**公共論戰性的**(大頭B、禿頭B、R. Incognito、盧子健、免治港人),意圖介入具體的政治/學術爭議,即使修辭激烈,底層仍預設一個「有可能被說服、被影響」的公共讀者;另一種是**私密宣洩性的**(GODOG、Beastmaster),寫作行為本身更接近自我治療或自我毀滅的儀式,發表與否、被理解與否,已不是主要考量。若這個區分成立,我先前把GODOG與Beastmaster都硬塞進「揭穿全能敘事」這個母題的做法,可能低估了這兩篇文本與其他五篇之間類別上的根本差異。
**五、"The Boxer"的引用:比GODOG的聖經引用更誠實地承認了「反抗的徒勞」**
值得特別注意的是Beastmaster結尾引用的〈The Boxer〉歌詞——「他一次又一次說『我要走了,我要走了』,但那個鬥士依然還在」。這句歌詞精準地捕捉了Beastmaster全文的核心矛盾:他用整篇文章宣告自己要離開、要「默默地離開學苑,逐漸枯乾」,但這個「宣告離開」的行為本身,恰恰是他還無法真正離開的證據——一個真正毫不在乎的人,不需要寫一篇長文來解釋自己的毫不在乎。這與GODOG最後那句「Aftermath」裡强行給出的、彷彿豁然開朗的神學收尾("鬧劇已經接近尾聲,基督將會第二次降臨")形成有趣對比:GODOG試圖用一個外部的、宗教的終末敘事來為自己混亂的內心掙扎畫下句點;Beastmaster則老實承認,自己所引用的這首歌本身就在說「離開的宣告」與「留下的事實」之間那個无法解决的裂縫——他沒有假裝自己已經想通,他只是誠實地把這個裂縫攤開給讀者看
## English
**I. A Confirmed Identity: Beastmaster Turns Out to Be the Drinking Companion from Big-Head B's "Perplexities"**
The most important discovery in this text is that it **confirms a lead we could previously only suspect**: Big-Head B, in "Perplexities," describes drinking with "Beastmaster," who, in his cups, uttered the lines "man must live by myth" and the warning about dialectic being abused. We now have Beastmaster's own essay, and it is saturated, start to finish, with exactly that tone — drunk, embittered, deeply hostile toward "myth" and "tradition": "I don't like tradition, and I don't want to leave one behind either," "don't tell me that without tradition nothing can continue." This forms a direct, verifiable intertext with the line Big-Head B attributes to him: Beastmaster despises how "myth" and "tradition" hold the individual hostage, yet knows full well he cannot escape the way this entire _Undergrad_ ideological apparatus has shaped his own emotional structure. The drinking companion Big-Head B describes as "either gone slightly mad or just drunk" now has a complete, self-confessional text to back him up — the two essays really do point to the same real person.
**II. A Direct Dialogue with R. Incognito: Beastmaster Personally Enacts the "Tragic Hero" and the "Deviant"**
This essay can almost be read as **a first-person confessional version** of R. Incognito's theory of the "paradigm/actor" in "The Theory of Life." R. Incognito writes, theoretically: "In almost every paradigm, when an actor moves to its margin or beyond it, they will be defined as a deviant." Beastmaster speaks from directly within that position: "By the time I entered _Undergrad_ I was already a ghost — I can appear or vanish at any time," "don't follow me, don't follow the veteran ghosts. Green ghosts have their own path." R. Incognito describes the "tragic hero" predicament of the "new culture people" in third-person, clinically superior psychoanalytic language; Beastmaster performs that very predicament, live, in raw first-person language with no theoretical packaging at all — "doing _Undergrad_ is like playing dominoes: once it gets big enough, it becomes unstoppable," "anyone who lasts long in _Undergrad_ is one of three things: an inhuman beast, an emotionless machine, or a narcissistic, willful big kid."
A striking contrast emerges here: R. Incognito theorizes the psychopathology of the "new culture people" with an air of clinical superiority; Beastmaster admits, without any concealment, that he is himself part of this pathological structure — even using language bordering on self-harm ideation ("sooner or later I'll end up like Lam Kwo-wan... except my first victim will be myself") to live out, unmediated by any theory, exactly the "thanatos" (death drive) R. Incognito discusses at arm's length.
**III. A Temperamental Opposite to Big-Head B: Two Utterly Different Versions of "Unlearnedness"**
Big-Head B's "unlearnedness" is a **strategic, gently self-mocking posture of modesty**, aimed at preserving room to speak without harming any specific individual. Beastmaster's posture is the exact opposite — not modesty, but **total nihilism and self-loathing**: "In truth I'm boring, worthless, sloppy as a person, no fun at all." This line resembles Big-Head B's self-deprecation on the surface, but its emotional temperature is entirely different: beneath Big-Head B's self-mockery lies a gentle, still-hopeful attitude toward public discourse (he does, after all, still "hope the Academic Section and the editors won't just toss this... in the wastebasket"). Beastmaster's self-loathing has abandoned all expectation of external response — the whole piece is saturated with a decisive exit posture: "mind your own business," "I'm done talking about the Council."
If Big-Head B represents the posture of "trying to be heard from the institution's margin," Beastmaster represents the posture of "having already given up on being heard, seeking only to disappear, gracefully or otherwise." The two men, in the same publication, at the same historical moment, present two utterly different emotional responses to the same structure of exclusion — one still knocking at the door, the other already turning away, knowing full well that "entering _Undergrad_ usually means suffering."
**IV. A Deep Resonance with GODOG: Two "Private" Texts Sharing the Same Genre of "Destructive Confession"**
In my earlier self-critique, I suggested GODOG's essay might be "a private, almost confessional piece of anxiety-writing," fundamentally different in genre from the other six "public-facing, deliberately interventionist" texts. Beastmaster's essay, to some degree, supports that judgment: it shares with GODOG a nearly reader-indifferent, almost self-destructive impulse toward confession, rather than carefully engineered polemical rhetoric. Both texts contain direct expressions of self-harm/self-destruction ideation (GODOG's "wet dream" and apocalyptic fantasy; Beastmaster's "like Lam Kwo-wan... my first victim will be myself"), and both quote an external text as a vehicle for emotional release (GODOG quotes scripture; Beastmaster quotes Paul Simon's "The Boxer").
This suggests that within this body of _Undergrad_ materials, there may be two fundamentally distinct axes of writing motivation: one **publicly polemical** (Big-Head B, Bald-Head B, R. Incognito, Lo Chi-kin, "Minced Hong Kong Person"), aimed at intervening in a specific political/academic controversy, and even at its most intense still presupposing a public reader who might conceivably be persuaded or moved; the other **privately cathartic** (GODOG, Beastmaster), where the act of writing itself functions closer to a ritual of self-therapy or self-destruction, and whether it is published or understood is no longer the primary concern. If this distinction holds, my earlier move of forcing both GODOG and Beastmaster into the same "exposing the omniscient narrative" motif may have underestimated a fundamental categorical difference between these two texts and the other five.
**V. The Citation of "The Boxer": A More Honest Acknowledgment of "the Futility of Resistance" than GODOG's Biblical Citation**
Worth particular attention is Beastmaster's closing citation of "The Boxer" — "I am leaving, I am leaving," but the fighter still remains. This lyric precisely captures the central contradiction of the entire essay: Beastmaster spends the whole piece declaring that he will leave, that he will "leave _Undergrad_ quietly, gradually drying up" — but the very act of declaring this departure is itself evidence that he cannot yet truly leave. Someone who genuinely didn't care wouldn't need to write a long essay explaining how little they cared. This makes for an interesting contrast with GODOG's forced, seemingly resolved theological closing in the "Aftermath" ("the farce is nearly at its end; Christ will come again a second time"): GODOG tries to use an external, religious eschatological narrative to draw a neat line under his own chaotic internal struggle; Beastmaster, by contrast, honestly admits that the very song he cites is itself about the unresolvable gap between "the declaration of leaving" and "the fact of staying" — he doesn't pretend to have figured it out. He simply lays that gap open for the reader to see..
